Validate arguments and return values

Source: R/validate.R
validate_args.Rd

Decorators that check a function's inputs or output against validators you supply. A validator is any function (or rlang::as_function() formula) that takes the value, so base predicates, lambdas and the check_*() functions of packages like checkmate all work, with no dependency on any of them.

Usage

validate_args(...)

validate_return(validator)

Arguments

...

For validate_args(), named validators, one per argument.

validator

For validate_return(), a validator for the returned value.

Value

A decorator.

Details

A validator passes if it returns exactly TRUE. It fails if it returns anything else:

  • a string, which becomes the failure message (the check_*() convention),

  • FALSE or any other value, which gives a generic message.

If a validator signals an error, that error propagates unchanged, so assert_*() style functions work too.

validate_args() checks the effective value of each named argument, so defaults are validated too. Checking forces the argument, so a validated argument is evaluated at call time rather than lazily. All failures are reported in one error of class fnware_validation_error. Validator names are checked against the function's formals when it is decorated, so a typo fails early.

Examples

f := validate_args(x = is.numeric, n = ~ .x > 0) %@% function(x, n = 1) x * n
f(2, 3)
#> [1] 6
try(f("a", -1))
#> Error : Invalid arguments.
#> ✖ `x`: failed validation.
#> ✖ `n`: failed validation.

# check_*() style validators return a message on failure
check_string <- function(x) if (is.character(x) && length(x) == 1) TRUE else "must be a string"
g := validate_args(name = check_string) %@% function(name) name
try(g(1))
#> Error : Invalid arguments.
#> ✖ `name`: must be a string

h := validate_return(is.character) %@% function() 1
try(h())
#> Error : Invalid return value.
#> ✖ failed validation.
